product_info.name: Wells Fargo Active Cash Credit Card

terms_analysis.key_information:
Key Points:
• APR ranges from 19.24% to 29.24% for purchases (variable rate based on creditworthiness), which is typical for mainstream credit cards
• No annual fee and 2% cash back on all purchases with no categories to track - simpler and more generous than most flat-rate cards
• Pro: 25+ day grace period means you pay zero interest if you pay your full balance each month
• Con: Balance transfer fee up to 5% is on the high end compared to cards offering 3% or promotional 0% transfer fees
terms_analysis.risks:
Potential Risks:
• [MEDIUM] Mandatory arbitration clause prevents class-action lawsuits and jury trials, though Wells Fargo won't use arbitration for debt collection. This is standard for most major credit cards.
  Impact: If you have a dispute, you must resolve it through private arbitration rather than court, which can limit your legal options
terms_analysis.consumer_score:
Credit Card Consumer Score: 58/100 (Mediocre)
Interpretation: This is an average mainstream credit card - the no annual fee and straightforward 2% cash back are positives, but the moderate-to-high APR range makes it costly if you carry a balance. Best for those who pay in full monthly.
terms_analysis.details:
Details:
• Interest rates: 19.24%-29.24% APR for purchases/balance transfers; 29.99% APR for cash advances
• Fees: No annual fee; up to $40 late payment fee; 5% balance transfer fee ($5 minimum); 5% cash advance fee ($10 minimum)
• Rewards: 2% unlimited cash back on all purchases with no earning caps or rotating categories
• Payment terms: Minimum payment is 1% of balance plus interest and fees, or $25 (whichever is greater)
• Grace period: At least 25 days to pay without interest on new purchases if you pay in full
• Foreign transactions: 3% fee on international purchases (standard for most cards)

reddit_insights.positive:
• 2% cash back on all purchases with no annual fee
• $200 welcome bonus and cell phone insurance included
• Easy redemption and potential future travel point transfers
reddit_insights.negative:
• 3% foreign transaction fee limits international travel use
• Credit limit increases can be difficult to obtain
• Tied to Wells Fargo, which some users distrust
